appearance.description: How the subject is identified in decoded raster when the component's design records do not supply it: the subject's solid identifying color. Raster identification never scans outside the declared subject region.

human_verdict.description: A recorded human judgment for a case whose judgment mode is human. Supplied at evaluation time; the evaluator incorporates it and labels the resulting assertion as human-sourced. It never originates from the evaluator itself.

judgment.description: automated: the evaluator's measurement families decide. human: the case names a semantic judgment automation must not fabricate; evaluation then requires an attached human verdict record and reports needs_human_judgment without one.

occlusion_checkpoint.description: One depth-evidence observation: the fraction of the subject expected to be visible at this frame because the named occluder passes in front of it (or it passes behind the occluder). A visible-fraction dip that returns to full visibility is raster proof of a front/back relationship; a subject drawn in front would measure full visibility throughout.

claims_depth.description: True when the beat claims front/back, containment, or perspective depth. A depth claim can only pass with occlusion or depth evidence (Section 7.1 row C10 minimum proof); the evaluator refuses it by name otherwise.

interval.description: The motion interval in the Section 5.4 half-open convention [start_frame, end_frame_exclusive). Required for linear_reveal, path_transit, and depth_transit; the full-fps clip is extracted over exactly this interval.

description: The MG-032 motion assertion schema. A motion proof case declares, for one required non-text motion beat, the named subject, the intended transformation, and the checkpoint states (initial, intermediate proof, final) at which the subject's geometry or identity must be confirmed in rendered frames. Expected geometry is derived from the scene specification at evaluation time (dataset and design records for chart components, resolved frame functions for diagram components); a case never grades its own homework. This schema is owned by MG-032 and lives beside, not inside, references/contracts-v2.schema.json: extending the canonical contracts schema belongs to the pending contracts revision. Evaluation semantics, verdict vocabulary, and exit-code mapping are defined in references/motion-proof.md and implemented in runtime/src/motion-proof.
title: Motion proof case (MG-032): semantic subject-motion assertions for one motion beat
